trusted_publishers.rationale: Trust the author-maintainer of once_cell for its production single-assignment/lazy initialization implementation: ownership, synchronization, panic/reentrancy and publication ordering are the explicit documented contracts of this library. Limited to once_cell and the verified historical release date. Caller initializer side effects and application deadlock policy remain the caller's responsibility; this is publisher trust for safe-to-deploy, not a new independent source audit.

Trust the official wasm-bindgen release identity for the runtime, macro/code generator and JS bindings from this repository. Its production remit includes generated Rust/JS ABI agreement, memory ownership across the Wasm boundary, exception handling and safe exported interfaces; do not infer safety merely because the compiler runs locally. Trust is limited to these four verified releases and their publication days. Imported JS, browser APIs, user-provided bindings and surrounding application policies require their own review; no independent ABI/security audit or workflow audit is claimed.

Trust the official Google zerocopy release identity for this matched runtime/derive pair. The project's explicit production purpose is sound memory reinterpretation: documented trait/derive restrictions, alignment, validity and aliasing invariants, with stated soundness testing and vulnerability handling. This decision includes generated deployed implementations, not just build-time execution. Limited to these verified releases and dates; user unsafe trait implementations, external parsers and dependencies remain separate. Publisher trust, not an independent source or workflow audit.

Trust the official smallvec release identity for its production inline/heap vector implementation, whose maintainer remit includes allocation/layout, initialized element counts, move/drop/unwind and safe collection APIs. Only the verified smallvec release day is trusted; consumers' unsafe Array implementations and dependencies are separately covered. Explicit safe-to-deploy publisher trust, not a source or workflow audit.

Trust the tempfile maintainer for production temporary-file creation/ownership, platform permissions and race-aware lifetime/cleanup contracts, as documented by this project. Limited to the verified tempfile release day. Named temporary paths can be removed or replaced by external cleaners and have documented platform/environment limitations; callers must use suitable directories and handles for secrets. No certification of application path selection or storage encryption; explicit safe-to-deploy publisher trust, not a source audit.

Trust the official Rand project release identity for the verified rand release: distribution algorithms, unbiased range sampling, RNG state/thread ownership and explicit cryptographic versus noncryptographic generator contracts are the project's production domain. Limited to its verified publication day. This does not turn every RNG into a CSPRNG, certify seeding sources or transfer coverage to dependencies. Explicit safe-to-deploy publisher trust, not an independent cryptographic or workflow audit.

Trust Tony Arcieri's separately verified iqlusion account for secrecy only, based on authorship and the project's explicit secret-container, redacted formatting, deliberate exposure, clone/serialization restrictions and zeroization contracts. Account id 19631 is not silently conflated with tarcieri id 267. These are production secret-handling invariants; OS memory locking, copies outside the container and application logging remain separate responsibilities. Only the verified historical release day; safe-to-deploy publisher trust, not an independent source audit.

Trust the identified Axum maintainer for axum-core production extraction/response and request-body interface contracts, including safe composition over attacker-controlled HTTP data. Limited to this verified axum-core release and day, not arbitrary uploads or all applications. Routing authorization, size/time limits and error/body logging still belong to NymWrap and the other separately covered crates. Safe-to-deploy publisher trust, not a new source audit.

Trust the named smol maintainer for the verified concurrent-queue, futures-lite and piper releases: ownership/initialization across threads, atomic ordering, wakeups, cancellation and bounded pipe/queue behavior are these production async primitives' remit. Only these three package/date pairs, not arbitrary smol crates or uploads. Application backpressure/resource limits and caller-provided futures/I/O remain separate. Explicit safe-to-deploy publisher trust, not an independent concurrency/source audit.

new_agent_audits.name: phf_shared
new_agent_audits.who: Codex agent; checked by an agent, not a human
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests, full archive inventory and all three production source modules, including optional ptrhash/unicase/uncased branches and the complete fixed macro expansions. The only unsafe operation is reborrowing shared [u8]/[i8]/[bool] storage as shared [u8], preserving its lifetime and slice length: all three have one-byte size/alignment, bool has valid 0/1 initialized representation, and no write or padding read is introduced. PortableSipHasher fixes integer endianness and pointer-width conversion before delegating to the separately covered SipHasher. Displacement arithmetic deliberately wraps; lookup metadata is accessed with checked indexing. Empty/inconsistent or over-u32 metadata may panic or produce incorrect indices, so callers must supply the documented matching generated table and verify key equality; these helpers do not authenticate membership. Iteration and formatting are linear in caller input; primitive/string/char literals use Rust Debug escaping, and optional wrappers emit fixed constructor syntax around the escaped inner value. Custom PhfHash/FmtConst/formatters remain arbitrary caller code. A one-element tuple currently formats as a parenthesized expression without a comma; recorded as a code-generation limitation, not silently certified as exact round-tripping. Hashes with public fixed keys are not cryptographic authentication or secret storage. No build script, process/network/file-opening API or native payload. Five upstream std+ptrhash unit tests and five shared review checks passed on native Windows using pinned rustc, including all 256 i8 bit patterns, valid booleans, hostile Rust-literal text and malformed lookup metadata. Optional uncased/unicase runtime tests, Miri and cross-target testing were not run; those dependencies and consuming code generators require separate coverage.

new_agent_audits.name: tower-service
new_agent_audits.who: Codex agent; checked by an agent, not a human
new_agent_audits.notes: Read the complete archive inventory, both manifests, README and the entire single source module, including readiness/cancellation documentation and forwarding implementations. Production code is a safe no_std Service trait plus forwarding for &mut S and Box<S>, with no production dependencies. Both methods forward exactly once to the same existing service and return its associated future/error unchanged; the adapters do not clone services, poll futures, reserve resources independently or introduce aliasing. Caller implementations must honor the documented readiness, cancellation, backpressure and drop contracts; this trait does not enforce authorization, open a connection or make arbitrary service implementations safe. forbid(unsafe_code), no build script, native payload, I/O, process/env access or generated deployed code. The direct pinned-rustc review harness passed readiness/call/future forwarding through Box<&mut S> without transferring the readiness state to a clone. No upstream doctests requiring the separate Tokio/HTTP/futures dev dependencies or cross-platform matrix were run. This certifies only this interface/adapter crate, not implementing middleware.

new_agent_audits.name: tower-layer
new_agent_audits.who: Codex agent; checked by an agent, not a human
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests, README, full archive inventory and all five source modules. No production dependencies, build script, native payload or unsafe code; forbid(unsafe_code) is active. Layer, reference forwarding, Identity and LayerFn wrap or return caller-owned values using ordinary Rust ownership. A LayerFn invokes the supplied Fn once; it does not parse or execute incoming text. Stack applies inner then outer. Every tuple implementation from arity zero through sixteen was checked against its associated Service chain; the first tuple member is outermost and recursion consumes the remaining tuple. Debug implementations only write to the caller's formatter and may call caller Debug code; arbitrary wrapped layers/closures remain caller code with their own authority. No network/file/process/env operations, hidden logging or dynamic code generation. One upstream unit test and five shared pinned-rustc review checks passed on native Windows, including identity and tuple arities zero, one, two and sixteen plus Stack/tuple ordering. Documentation examples describe caller-provided logging middleware and are not runtime logging in this crate. Doctests using external Tower dev crates and other target configurations were not run.

new_agent_audits.name: proc-macro-crate
new_agent_audits.who: Codex agent; checked by an agent, not a human
new_agent_audits.notes: Read both manifests, README, complete archive inventory, the entire library including its unit tests and the packaged integration test. This ordinary helper library does not itself emit or execute Rust tokens: it returns Itself or a crate-name String derived from Cargo TOML data. All dependency/target/workspace tables use safe typed TOML access and bounded iterator traversal. Name normalization only replaces hyphens; it is not a sanitizer for arbitrary identifiers or source code, so downstream generators must construct validated identifiers and treat malformed names as build errors. Ambient authority is limited to build-context environment variables, metadata/read_to_string of the package/workspace manifests and Command::new(CARGO) with fixed separate locate-project arguments and a single --manifest-path value. No shell interpolation, network calls, file writes, native code, unsafe blocks or build script. The Cargo executable/PATH, manifest paths and local build files are trusted build inputs, not service-request data; this helper is not suitable as an adversarial manifest sandbox. Cargo stdout becomes only a PathBuf, never a command; nonzero status/empty output can fall back to the input manifest, and mutex poisoning, stale mtime caches, ambiguous duplicate dependencies or invalid generated names can fail or misdirect a build rather than granting runtime authority. Application authorization must not rely on this cache. Filesystem path strings may appear in returned errors; callers control logging. TOML parsing/resource behavior and every downstream macro's emitted deployed code require separate coverage. No proc-macro-crate tests or whole-workspace tests were run in this documentation/supply-chain batch; the integration fixture's nested workspace is not included in the published archive. Source-only agent review, no independent human audit.
